extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of literary theory, literary critics, and readers applying Barthes' methods to texts
extracted.subtask_description: Using Roland Barthes' S/Z framework to analyze literary texts via five interwoven codes (hermeneutic, proairetic, semantic, symbolic, cultural), their voices, and their relations; emphasizes annotation and preserving textual plurality. Applicable to close readings and semiotic/narratological critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic code (HER.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The hermeneutic code concerns enigmas of the text: puzzles and mysteries that may or may not be answered, with final resolution deferred or misdirected—thus keeping the reader guessing. Barthes marks enigmas with 'HER.' (short for hermeneutic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barthes breaks the process of revealing truth into a sequence: Thematisation (what is an enigma?), Positioning (confirmations), Formulation of the enigma, Promise of an answer, Fraud (circumvention), Equivocation (mixture of fraud and truth), Blocking (enigma cannot be solved), Suspended answer, Partial answer, Disclosure of the truth. Because it moves from question to answer it is 'irreversible'—once revealed it cannot be unrevealed. The hermeneutic encompasses larger narrative questions compared to proairetic's detailed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proairetic (action) code (ACT.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proairetic code (action code) encompasses actions or small scene-like sequences in the narrative which create narrative tension and forward drive; Barthes marks these units 'ACT.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small units (e.g., 'had been sleeping' -> anticipate waking) build expectation; from these units the narrative acquires forward movement. This code connects to the 'readerly' text where the reader assimilates pieces of information in order. It constitutes location with spatial and temporal dimensions. Like the hermeneutic, it is irreversible: actions and their consequences cannot be undone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic (semic) code (SEM.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The semantic (or semic; 'SEM.') code concerns connotative meanings related to character—the 'resonances' beyond literal denotation that help develop themes across the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantic signifiers include name, costume, physical appearance, psychological traits, speech, and lexis; these signifiers carry unstable meanings and enable evolving character construction and thematic development. The semantic code is one of the reversible codes and supplies layered connotations that a reader may invoke differently across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic code (SYM.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The symbolic ('SYM.') code produces an accumulating structure of (often paired) symbolic meanings that establish a larger framework within which story meanings unfold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic clusters are often organized around oppositions (male/female, inside/outside, hidden/revealed, hot/cold). In Sarrasine Barthes identifies rhetorical (antitheses), sexual (castration), and economic (origin of wealth) transgressions as key symbolic processes. The symbolic structure is not stable; the 'writerly' reader pursues these structures until they break down—a symbolic collapse that is part of textual pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural code (REF.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cultural code ('REF.') refers to meanings external to the text—points where the text invokes common bodies of knowledge or axiomatic truths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes references to real-world places or asserted axioms (Barthes' example: the Faubourg Saint-Honoré; the opening sentence asserting that all men daydream at parties—a 'gnomic code'). Use of cultural code ties the text to external knowledge systems and shared background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes as voices and stereographic space
rubrics_metrics.description: Each code behaves like a 'voice' in a stereographic space: the codes are not superimposed but approximate something intrinsic to the text; together they 'weave' the text and can each dominate at times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Barthes maps voices to codes: proairetic = Voice of Empirics; semic/semantic = Voice of the Person; cultural = Voice of Science; hermeneutic = Voice of Truth; symbolic = Voice of Symbol. Treat codes as different off-stage commentaries that together form a network of interpretation rather than a single authoritative reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversibility vs. irreversibility of codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes distinguishes two irreversible codes (hermeneutic and proairetic) which move narrative forward in a way that cannot be undone, and three reversible codes (semantic, symbolic, cultural) which structure meaning but can be invoked or reconfigured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing a text, note which elements effect permanent cognitive change (answers, actions) versus those that generate mutable interpretive resonances. This distinction affects how codes interact and the reader's experience of closure or openness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve textual plurality / avoid privileging a single integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes insists on the plurality (multivalence) of the text: reading is plural and a different reader might invoke/combine the codes differently; modern 'plural' texts do not enforce a single model of integrating the codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing the text to one privileged interpretation. Do not impose an overall structure that 'closes' meaning; instead, show how codes open virtual digressions and permit multiple readings. The analyst's role is to map code occurrences, not to impose final closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation practice / systematic notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Barthes methodically moves through the text, denoting where and how different codes function and systematically notes and explains their usage as they occur (e.g., marking HER., ACT., SEM., SYM., REF.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt Barthes' practice of sequentially annotating textual units, cataloguing units as virtual digressions toward other units, and using shorthand code markers. Use annexed outlines (Barthes' Annexes) to summarize occurrences and relationships; treat units as prompts toward a catalogue of interpretive possibilities rather than closed meanings.
